intro: をものともせず comes from 物ともしない, "not even treat it as something". A serious obstacle stands in the way, and the subject treats it as nothing and pushes through. It is a phrase of admiration, used in writing, news and speeches about other people's courage.

skills.rule: A をものともせず(に) B: treating hardship A as nothing, the subject bravely does B.
skills.explain:
をものともせず (also をものともせずに) follows a noun for a difficulty: 怪我, 病気, 嵐, 危険, 困難, 批判, 年齢. The rest of the sentence is an achievement or a determined action that actually took place. The writer admires the subject.

Three limits matter. It reports what someone did or does; it is not used for requests, invitations or plans (×頑張ってください). It praises, so it is not used about yourself. And A must be a real obstacle; an ordinary circumstance does not count.

The neighbour most often confused is をよそに: there the subject ignores other people's worries or wishes, and the tone is cool or critical. にもかかわらず is a neutral "despite" that can be used in any statement, including about yourself.
patterns: [obstacle: injury / danger / storm / criticism] をものともせず(に)、[brave achievement]

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は足[あし]の怪我[けが]{をものともせず}、最後[さいご]まで走[はし]った。
examples.en: Undaunted by his leg injury, he ran to the very end.

examples.jp: 選手[せんしゅ]たちは激[はげ]しい雨[あめ]{をものともせず}、試合[しあい]を続[つづ]けた。
examples.en: The players carried on with the match in defiance of the heavy rain.

examples.jp: 救助隊[きゅうじょたい]は危険[きけん]{をものともせず}、雪[ゆき]の山[やま]に入[はい]った。
examples.en: Heedless of the danger, the rescue team went into the snowy mountains.

examples.jp: 祖母[そぼ]は高齢[こうれい]{をものともせず}、毎日[まいにち]畑[はたけ]で働[はたら]いている。
examples.en: Not letting her great age stop her, my grandmother works in the fields every day.

examples.jp: 博士[はかせ]は度重[たびかさ]なる失敗[しっぱい]{をものともせずに}、研究[けんきゅう]を続[つづ]けた。
examples.en: Undeterred by repeated failures, the scientist kept on with the research.

contrast.note: をよそに ignores other people's concerns (親の心配をよそに) and often criticises. をものともせず beats a hardship and praises. With 批判 both work, and the tone decides: brave persistence is をものともせず, ignoring people is をよそに.
にもかかわらず is a neutral "despite" for any statement, including about yourself and outcomes nobody chose: 雨にもかかわらず試合は行われた.

mistakes.bad: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]{をものともせず}頑張[がんば]ってください。
mistakes.good: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]でも頑張[がんば]ってください。
mistakes.note: It describes what someone has done or does; it cannot be a request.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]は高[たか]い熱[ねつ]{をものともせず}、試験[しけん]を受[う]けた。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]は高[たか]い熱[ねつ]があった{にもかかわらず}、試験[しけん]を受[う]けた。
mistakes.note: It praises, so it is not used about yourself; say it neutrally with にもかかわらず.

mistakes.bad: 親[おや]の心配[しんぱい]{をものともせず}、息子[むすこ]は一人[ひとり]で旅[たび]に出[で]た。
mistakes.good: 親[おや]の心配[しんぱい]{をよそに}、息子[むすこ]は一人[ひとり]で旅[たび]に出[で]た。
mistakes.note: Parents' worry is not a hardship to overcome but a concern ignored: をよそに.

skills.tip: Would a newspaper call it heroic? Hardship beaten, admired: をものともせず.
